evidence.quote: Relational Migrator is only compatible with Snapshot migration jobs.

To run a snapshot migration repeatedly on a cadence, such as daily, use the Relational Migrator [REST API](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/relational-migrator/api-docs.md#std-label-rm-rest-api) with a task scheduler.
During one-time or continuous replication, you can automatically transform data by using rules to map the columns in your relational database to MongoDB fields.
Relational Migrator depends on an open-source Debezium connector to efficiently track row-level changes from the Oracle database in real-time.
- Continuous sync (CDC) migration mode

edits.rationale: MongoDB's Getting Started page says Relational Migrator is compatible only with snapshot jobs, which run once, and that repeating on a cadence means calling the REST API from a task scheduler, so each run is a separate job. AWS Prescriptive Guidance still mentions continuous replication, and Estuary's Oracle guide describes Relational Migrator CDC via Debezium. These are third-party descriptions; the 1.15 release notes show CDC was moved out of the tool. The advice to use current MongoDB docs is a recommendation, not a checkable fact.
